_comment: THE SUB-SESSION REGISTRY. One row per sub-session a manager has spawned.
WHY IT EXISTS, measured 2026-09-01: the two sub-sessions below existed ONLY
in the manager session's context. Had that session ended, nothing in the
repo named them -- no successor could have polled them, and both would have
been silently orphaned mid-work. This file is what makes a manager arriving
COLD able to resume rather than re-derive.
IT IS A REGISTRY, NOT A CHANNEL. A manager CANNOT message a sub-session:
SendMessage to a live sub-session id returns 'No agent named ... is
reachable', and there is no send_message or list_events tool. Verified by
test, not assumed. So a successor's only moves are: read this file, poll
each id with get_session, act on its branch/PR, and archive it when its
READ last_observed AS A SNAPSHOT, NEVER AS LIVE STATE. A sub-session's
needs_action is written at ITS last turn and cannot be cleared by the
manager handling the request. Phase C's still read 'open PR ... 403' long
after the PR was open. Poll get_session for current state; this file says
what EXISTS, not what is true right now.
